ceiling_policy: A ceiling is a statement about one artifact built by one cross toolchain, and the toolchain it was taken with is named in each row's budget.measured.comment. `text_bytes` is the summed .text of every emitted translation unit; `state_bytes` is sizeof(<Model>State) for the target ABI; both are bytes. Ceilings are fall-only in spirit: when size work lands, lower the ceiling in the same change that lands the saving, so the saving cannot be quietly spent again. Raising a ceiling is not forbidden but is never routine, and needs a reviewed justification recorded in the row's comment saying what grew and why the growth is worth the flash. The initial ceilings sit about four percent above the measurement recorded beside them: real headroom for ordinary churn, still tight enough that a five percent regression is red.
fp_ops_policy: `fp_ops` is the number of single-precision floating-point arithmetic instructions in a row's compiled objects, read from `arm-none-eabi-objdump -d` and summed over every emitted translation unit. It counts work, not traffic: the products and fused products, the sums, and the divide and square root. Moves, loads, stores, compares, conversions, sign flips, selections and roundings are excluded. The exact counted set has one owner, the gate's `fp_ops` module, and a single-precision mnemonic in neither its counted nor its excluded list fails the row rather than being counted as free. Bytes say whether the artifact fits; this number is what says whether the step makes its rate on a 600 MHz Cortex-M7 against a 1 ms period, so it is fall-only in the same sense as the size ceilings and for a sharper reason: when contraction work lands, these ceilings come down severalfold in the same change, and a later lowering that reintroduces quartic arithmetic is then red here instead of on the vehicle. The initial ceilings sit about four percent above the measurement recorded beside them.

entries.why: The artifact that flies: the RDD2 navigation estimator as GALEC-derived embedded C, linked into the Zephyr image on the vehicle's microcontroller. Its flash footprint and its single static allocation are acceptance criteria for that deployment, not diagnostics.

measured.comment: Re-measured 2026-08-24 after the fixed-count kernel work landed, with gcc-arm-embedded-15.2.rel1 under arm-none-eabi-gcc -Os -std=c99 -mcpu=cortex-m7 -mfpu=fpv5-d16 -mfloat-abi=hard -ffunction-sections -c over both emitted translation units. text 58648 B = 57214 B model + 1434 B shared kernels (was 59384 = 59216 + 168): the model unit shed 2002 B because the hot contraction loop nests now print as calls into the shared library's fixed-count kernels (copy/fill/dot/scaled-add at the run lengths 3/6/12/15/24), the fissioned first-pass products print in the transposed scaled-add form, guarded rectangular block assignments print with their loops restricted to the guard's own rectangle, and the shared library carries the straight-line specializations once for every artifact. state 31980 B unchanged. fp_ops 1094 = 1023 model + 71 shared kernels (was 1144 = 1142 + 2): the drop is real arithmetic removed, chiefly the row-scale coefficients that were re-multiplied per element and now multiply once per contracted step. Behavior witness: the dossier-rig host driver (40 warm steps, one GPS pos+vel dostep, scenario 6) produces byte-identical status, NIS and output report before and after, and the dynamically executed worst-step instruction count fell from 954168 to 572366 (model-A upper bound, dyn.pl over both TUs). Ceilings LOWERED in the same change that lands the saving, per the fall-only policy: text 61455 -> 61000, fp 1184 -> 1138 (about four percent above the new measurements).

entries.why: The same estimator inside its eFMU Production Code container, the form the certification review reads. Its C bodies come from the same shared templates as the embedded-c-galec row, so the two rows are pinned to the same numbers on purpose: a divergence between them means the packaging track changed what gets compiled rather than only how it is wrapped, which is a finding either way.

measured.comment: Re-measured 2026-08-24 after the fixed-count kernel work landed, with gcc-arm-embedded-15.2.rel1 under the same flags as the embedded-c-galec row, over ProductionCode/. Byte-identical to that row's measurement by construction: galec-production extends the same C templates and overrides only the conformance banner, which is a comment. It therefore carries that row's numbers and lowered ceilings unchanged (text 61455 -> 61000, fp 1184 -> 1138), so the two artifacts cannot drift apart without one of them going red. See the embedded-c-galec row's comment for the measured split and the behavior witness.

entries.why: The heaviest matrix-algebra model with an established eFMI target, and nearly as large as the navigation estimator despite being a smaller model: sigma-point work is where an unrolled kernel or a widened scratch region shows up first, so this row is the early warning for both ceilings.

measured.comment: Re-measured 2026-08-24 after the fixed-count kernel work landed, same toolchain and flags as the NavigationEstimator rows, over ProductionCode/. text 55334 B (was 56962), state 31292 B unchanged, fp_ops 1301 (was 1322): the sigma-point loop nests pick up the same kernelized emission, a smaller win than the estimator's because fewer of its contractions sit at the specialized run lengths. Ceilings LOWERED with the saving, per the fall-only policy: text 59155 -> 57550, fp 1374 -> 1353.

entries.why: The other artifact that flies, and the one on the fast loop: the RDD2 attitude and rate controller as GALEC-derived embedded C, running beside the navigation estimator on the same microcontroller and against a shorter period. It is gated from the day its cross-compile is warning-free on both targets, because a controller that fits only when the estimator happens to be small is not a deployment anyone can plan; its own ceilings say so independently. It is also the corpus's densest user of the Lie-group function library, so a region overlay or a call-boundary decision that regresses on nested small functions shows up here before it shows up on the estimators.

measured.comment: Re-measured 2026-08-24 after the fixed-count kernel work landed, same toolchain and flags. text 20892 B = 19458 B model + 1434 B shared kernels (was 19788 = 19620 + 168); fp_ops 402 = 331 model + 71 shared kernels (was 336 = 334 + 2); state 3860 B unchanged. CEILING RAISED (text 20579 -> 21730, fp 349 -> 418), reviewed justification: the model unit itself SHRANK (162 B text, 3 fp instructions), and the entire growth is the shared kernel library's fixed-count specializations, which this gate sums into every row because it measures per-artifact objects. The library is byte-identical for every artifact of one compiler build, so an image that links the controller beside the estimator carries ONE copy, and -ffunction-sections plus --gc-sections drops the specializations nothing in the image calls; the summed-object number is therefore an upper bound the deployment does not pay twice. The specializations exist for the 1 kHz estimator budget (worst correcting step 954168 -> 572366 executed instructions, measured with the dossier rig) and the controller shares the identical library bytes by design rather than growing any code of its own.

entries.why: The same controller inside its eFMU Production Code container, pinned against the embedded-c-galec row's numbers for the reason the two NavigationEstimator rows are pinned against each other: the C bodies come from the same shared templates, so a divergence means the packaging track changed what gets compiled rather than only how it is wrapped.

measured.comment: Re-measured 2026-08-24 after the fixed-count kernel work landed, with gcc-arm-embedded-15.2.rel1 under the same flags as the flight-controller/embedded-c-galec row, over ProductionCode/. Byte-identical to that row's measurement by construction: galec-production extends the same C templates and overrides only the conformance banner, which is a comment. It carries that row's raised ceilings and their recorded justification unchanged (the growth is the shared fixed-count kernel library, deduplicated and link-time garbage-collected in a real image; the model unit itself shrank), so the two artifacts cannot drift apart without one of them going red.
